composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate required fields first, so a missing/blank field is a 400 listing the
# offending field names before any entity is built or persisted.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateNewOwner
  next: uniqueTelephone

# Reject a create whose normalized telephone is already used by another owner (409),
# before any entity is built or persisted.
uniqueTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateUniqueTelephone
  next: uniqueEmail

# Reject a create whose lower-cased email is already used by another owner (409),
# before any entity is built or persisted. An absent email is never a conflict.
uniqueEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateUniqueEmail
  next: uniqueHousehold

# A household is same last name at the same address (case-insensitive, whitespace collapsed).
# Read-only gate: reject a create that joins an existing household with a 409, unless the
# request set 'sharesHousehold' true — in which case it publishes the household's stable
# 'householdId' for the steps below. Runs before any entity is built or persisted.
uniqueHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateUniqueHousehold
  next: cityCapacity

# Reject a create whose city already contains 50 or more owners with a 409, before any
# entity is built or persisted.
cityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateCityCapacity
  next: dailyLimit

# Reject a create once 100 or more owners have already been created today (by
# registrationDate) with a 429, before any entity is built or persisted.
dailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateDailyOwnerLimit
  next: applyHousehold

# When joining a shared household, back-fill the published 'householdId' onto existing members
# so the whole household carries the same id. A no-op otherwise.
applyHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ApplySharedHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

# Emit the audit line after the owner is saved (id populated) and before responding,
# keeping the audit side effect in its own step rather than in the responder.
audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: bulkWarning

# Populate the response-only bulkSignupWarning flag from the count of owners created today
# (this owner is now saved and counted).
bulkWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagBulkSignup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'

          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when not supplied. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag. When true, allows creating this owner even though another
            owner has the same last name at the same address (same household); otherwise
            such a create is rejected with 409.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:

The implementation is complete and the test suite is green. Here's a summary of what I did.

## What changed

Duplicate detection is now a single derived **`identityKey`** = `normalizedTelephone + "|" + (email or "") + "|" + (householdId or "")`, and a create is rejected with **409** only when a new owner's *whole* key equals an existing owner's.

**New files**
- `OwnerIdentity.java` — single source of truth building the key from normalized parts (`key(...)`) and deriving an existing owner's key (`of(owner)`, re-normalizing stored telephone/email).
- `ValidateUniqueIdentity.java` — the one duplicate gate: derives the new owner's key (using the request's already-normalized telephone/email and the resolved household id) and rejects on an exact full-key collision.
- `DuplicateIdentityException` + handler + escalation YAML (→ 409).
- `ResolveHousehold.java` — the former `ValidateUniqueHousehold`, now only *resolves and publishes* the shared `Household.Id` (no rejection).

**Removed** (their logic is now folded into the one key): `ValidateUniqueTelephone`, `ValidateUniqueEmail`, `ValidateUniqueHousehold`, and the `DuplicateTelephone/Email/Household` exceptions, handlers, and escalation YAMLs.

**Updated**
- `owners.POST.yml`: pipeline is now `validate → resolveHousehold → uniqueIdentity → cityCapacity → …`.
- `BuildOwner` stamps the key onto the entity; `RespondWithOwner` (GET) derives it too, so every owner response carries `identityKey`.
- `Owner` model: transient `identityKey` + accessors.
- `openapi.yml`: added readOnly `identityKey` to the `Owner` schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` and MapStruct mapper return it), and marked `sharesHousehold` deprecated/ignored.

## Behaviour change (as specified)
Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same `householdId`) with **different** telephones derive **different** keys and are both allowed — only an exact full-key match is a duplicate. The former separate telephone/email/household 409s no longer fire on their own.

The acceptance test `coreRejectsIdentityCollision` (two otherwise-unique owners sharing a telephone → both get key `+61…||` → 409) passes, and `mvn test` reports `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 — BUILD SUCCESS`.

One scoping note: the create and single-owner GET responses populate `identityKey`; the list and PUT responders still map the entity directly (they'd serialize `identityKey` as absent/null), which I left untouched since the spec centers on the create's duplicate detection. Say the word if you'd like those populated too.
